weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions (numbers from the menu in view), the main action (number noted from this run's main-action menu) and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: The batched quarter depends on main-action numbers the agent saw in an earlier quarter. If the menu order or numbering changes, the agent will pick the wrong action without noticing, and only the success flag might catch it. This weakens robustness when the order changes.
weaknesses.fix: Tell the agent to read the main-action number from the menu shown in the current quarter, or to confirm the action name in the result. If the label does not match the intended action, it should observe and choose again.

weaknesses.quote: in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began, judged on the stats held at that moment. This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: The review calendar is built on a timing observation that differs from the handbook's order, where the review comes after the quarterly phase. The 'Review in N' formula then carries a manual override. Together these make the most important deadline logic ambiguous and possibly wrong under the official configuration.
weaknesses.fix: Define the review deadline by game signals. Protect the stats from month 5 (11, 17…) until the review or performance-talk event has actually resolved, whatever the month count, and drop the claim about timing from 'our runs'.

weaknesses.quote: **Review-month exception** (Review in 1, HR remark friendly or quiet, not in a stalled start): apply step 4 first. A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable
weaknesses.problem: Step 4 is placed above step 2 only some of the time, and that conflicts with the stated priority 'stay in the run … no second hidden-risk blow-up'. Combined with very long, nested lists of cue words, this makes the story procedure hard for a flash model to apply consistently.
weaknesses.fix: Keep one fixed order: Survive, then Risk, then Wellbeing, then Review, then Grow. Express the review concern as a tie-break inside the low-risk options, and shorten the cue lists to 3–4 representative verbs per stat.

weaknesses.quote: This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months (Review in 1) and protects Skill, Network and Output through them
weaknesses.problem: The rulebook puts the review after the quarterly phase in months 6, 12, 18 and so on. The Skill moves the review a month earlier based on its own run observations. This changes the status-line formula, step 4 and the review-month risk exception, so the whole review plan rests on a timing claim the rules do not publish. If the official configuration follows the handbook order, the agent protects the wrong month and takes 'mild risk' in the wrong month.
weaknesses.fix: Base the default on the published timing: the review happens at the end of months 6, 12, 18 and so on, after the quarterly phase. Protect both the month before and the review month itself. Keep the earlier-review observation only as a fallback that applies when the review talk actually shows up at the start of a month.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply ... From the second quarter on, send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions (numbers from the menu in view), the main action (number noted from this run's main-action menu) and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: A large share of the Skill is about tool-call batching for token efficiency, not career strategy. Sending the main action blind, using an option number copied from an earlier quarter's note, is fragile. A model can easily pick the wrong action if menu numbering or the phase order changes. That hurts both clarity and robustness.
weaknesses.fix: Shorten the turn loop to a few lines. Before choosing a main action, always check its number against the menu currently shown, and only batch actions when every option number is visible in the current observe result. Move the token-saving details into an appendix.

weaknesses.quote: Main action Apply for rotation.
weaknesses.problem: From L4 up the Skill says 'Skill first, Output second', but every quarter it picks a main action that has no published Output effect. That leaves Output resting on one Prepare-report point, against the stated priority. There is also no rule for switching main actions using the review grade, even though the handbook says two weak reviews mean dismissal.
weaknesses.fix: Alternate the main action at L4+: Apply for rotation or Build a mentorship when Skill is the stat under its Best, and Apply for a key project or Report results to your manager when Output or Network lags. After any C or D grade, switch to Apply for a key project with the Energy split across Prepare report materials until the next review.

weaknesses.quote: Anything below said to happen "in our runs" or "usually" is our own observation, not a game rule
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is long and dense, and it mixes published rules with the author's own run observations and invented specifics. Examples are "in our runs a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed", "one point of Network or Output lost in the review month cost the first promotion", and the claim that Output lags at the starting level. They are hedged, but they still drive the numeric branching. A 3B-class or flash model will struggle to apply the nested step 1-5 logic, the strict mode, the review-month exception and the stalled-start rule consistently, and the unverified claims can mislead it.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the Skill to roughly a third of its length. Keep a short priority ladder: survive, then risk, then wellbeing, then review, then grow. Keep one table for the quarterly actions. Delete the anecdotal "in our runs" claims or move them into one clearly labelled heuristics list.

weaknesses.quote: **Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it:** reply 1 is `new_game`; reply 2 is `observe`; reply 3 answers the opening screen
weaknesses.problem: The Skill spends a lot of space on call batching and the reply protocol, such as the pair of `take_action` + `observe`, "two replies in the first quarter, one reply from the second on", and "Never send `observe` in a reply of its own". This is mechanics tuned to the author's own runs, and it rests on assumptions about the harness that may not hold, such as the menu order and the menu numbers. It crowds out the strategy, and a menu that differs from what was assumed will break it.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the turn loop to a few lines: observe, choose, take_action, observe. State once that the model should read the menu numbers from the latest observation and never assume them. Drop the first-quarter versus later-quarter split.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..>
weaknesses.problem: The review-timing model is invented and is presented as a rule: "N = 6 - (current_month mod 6)", and the claim that reviews appear as months 6, 12 … begin. It contradicts the handbook ordering, in which the review comes after the quarterly phase. The cue-based effect guesses for Skill, Output and Network are assumptions that may not hold under different event wording. The compulsory status-line note adds overhead and a way to fail.
weaknesses.fix: Say only that a review comes every 6 months, and that Skill, Network and Output should be kept healthy continuously, with a mild extra push for Output and Network in the month or two before a review. Make the status note optional, or reduce it to a short free-text stat summary. Mark every effect guess as a fallback to be overridden by the observed stat deltas.

weaknesses.quote: Reviews come every six months (handbook). The handbook lists the review after the quarterly phase; in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began
weaknesses.problem: Relies on unpublished, run-specific observations (review timing, 'one point of Network or Output lost cost the first promotion', 'dismissed at month 24') and presents them as guidance. These are invented or unverifiable mechanics that may not hold, and they add hedging that conflicts with the handbook's order.
weaknesses.fix: Remove run-specific anecdotes and the month-5/11/17 review-month heuristic. State only published facts (review every 6 months, after the quarterly phase). Say to keep Skill, Network and Output rising steadily before each review. Keep any calendar rule only if marked as a heuristic, in one sentence.

weaknesses.quote: Reread this Skill whenever its rules are not in view ... Then apply these steps in order. Skip a step if it would remove every option. ... Review-month exception (Review in 1, HR remark friendly or quiet, not in a stalled start): apply step 4 first.
weaknesses.problem: Very long, with deeply nested conditionals, exceptions to exceptions, and cross-references between sections (strict mode, stalled start, review-month exception, N=1/N=2). A flash-class model will struggle to apply it consistently, and the protocol overhead (status line, tool-call choreography) buries the strategy.
weaknesses.fix: Cut to about one third of the length. Use a single ordered priority list (survive, risk, wellbeing, review prep, grow) with one threshold per stat. Move the turn-loop and note-format mechanics to a short separate section, and drop the nested exceptions.

weaknesses.quote: **Skill** rises when you use your own judgement: analyse, bring data or evidence ... **Output** rises when you deliver, ship, finish ... **Hidden risk** ... challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: Gives detailed keyword-to-effect mappings that are presented as working assumptions but are not in the rules, and they are brittle. Wording changes break the mapping, and some are arbitrary (reporting a concrete problem lowers risk, but a formal challenge raises it). This weakens robustness, and some of it reads close to event-specific guidance.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the cue lists with a generic method. Use the stat changes the game shows after each choice. Prefer options that clearly improve the lagging stat and avoid concealment or shortcuts. Treat unknown effects as unknown and pick the more transparent, reversible option.

weaknesses.quote: This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months (Review in 1) and protects Skill, Network and Output through them
weaknesses.problem: The published order puts the six-month review after the quarterly phase of months 6, 12, 18 and so on. This Skill replaces that with timing from its own runs. It then builds the status-line formula, the step-4 review protection and the 'Review-month exception' on that timing. If the official setup follows the handbook, the protection lands on the wrong month and the risk exception is spent in the wrong place.
weaknesses.fix: Make the published timing the default: the review follows the quarterly phase of months 6, 12, 18 and so on. Protect stats in months 5 and 6 together. Shift the window only if the review talk is actually seen earlier in this run.

weaknesses.quote: Levels 2 and 3:** Energy: Prepare report materials, Network maintenance, Prepare report materials (start with Network maintenance when Network is under its Best). Main action Apply for a key project.
weaknesses.problem: At levels 1 to 3 the Energy actions never buy Skill. Skill can come only from stories and the key-project main action. 'Skill falling materially behind' is a published failure, and the promotion bar rises with Skill, so a long run can stall or end in 'Obsolete'. There is also no check on whether Skill is keeping up.
weaknesses.fix: Add a rule tied to the trend: if Skill rose by 1 or less over the last two quarters, or is under its Best, swap two report points for Skill learning while Health is above 5. Every few quarters at L2–L3, use Build a mentorship or Apply for rotation as the main action instead of the key project.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order, and every result comes back before your next turn.
weaknesses.problem: About a third of the file covers token-saving reply shapes, batching numbered menus and a status-line formula with Best tracking. This is dense harness detail that a flash model can get wrong, for example by guessing menu numbers when batching a whole quarter. It also pushes the strategy down the page and makes the Skill harder to follow.
weaknesses.fix: Shrink the turn loop to three bullets: take_action + observe together, read the menu before a quarterly choice, keep a one-line note. Cut the Status line section to 'Review in N | S N O'. Drop Best tracking or replace it with 'compare with last note'. Move token-efficiency rationale to design/.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order, and every result comes back before your next turn.
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is long and dense. The token-saving turn loop, the status-line rules, the five-step story filter with its sub-modes (strict mode, the review-month exception, stalled start) and six quarterly lines all compete for attention. A flash-class model may misapply the nested exceptions or drop the two-call reply pattern partway through the run.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the Turn loop down to the reply template plus one fallback rule. Merge 'Strict mode', 'Review-month exception' and 'Stalled start' into one small decision table keyed on the HR remark tone and Review-in-N. Move the long wording-cue lists to the end of the file as a reference.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk ... is likely to rise with ... challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: The Skill treats unpublished mechanics as firm decision rules: the HR remark as the only risk gauge, reviews firing at the start of months 6, 12 and so on, and dismissal at month 24 if still at the starting level. The 'in our runs' hedges help, but the drop rules are absolute, so if the organisers' configuration differs, the agent will reject options that may be good ones (for example, formal escalation).
weaknesses.fix: Make these heuristics soft tie-breakers rather than 'drop' filters wherever the handbook says nothing. Keep hard drops only for published failure directions and for clear concealment, denial or blaming. Add one line telling the agent to update its working assumptions once the observed outcomes contradict them.

weaknesses.quote: Level 4 or above: ... Energy: Skill learning (2) while Health is above 5 ... Main action Apply for rotation.
weaknesses.problem: From L4 onward the plan is a single fixed recipe tuned to past runs. It never uses the Output-raising main actions, spends Health every quarter on Skill learning, and has no rule for reacting to performance grades. A C grade puts the run on the published 'two weak reviews' failure path, yet no quarterly line covers it. Wealth and the late-game balance across the ending dimensions are also not weighed.
weaknesses.fix: Add a quarterly line above the level lines: after a C or D grade, or when Output is under its Best, use Report results to your manager or Showcase results plus Prepare report materials until the next review is B or better. Rotate the main action according to whichever of Skill, Network or Output lags its Best.

weaknesses.quote: The handbook lists the review after the quarterly phase; in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began ... This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: The review timing rests on an observation from past runs, not on the published rules, and it conflicts with the handbook's order of events. Month-parity rules like 'Review in N' and the 'month 47 exception' depend on it. If the observation is wrong, the whole review-protection scheme is mistimed. The Skill also admits it is guessing.
weaknesses.fix: Follow the published order, with the review at the end of months 6, 12 and so on, after the quarterly phase. Keep one simple rule: protect Skill, Network and Output in the quarter before each review. Drop the 'in our runs' timing claims or move them into a clearly labelled hint that the game's own events override.

weaknesses.quote: Skill** rises when you use your own judgement: analyse, bring data or evidence ... **Hidden risk** (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately ... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: These long lists of keyword cues are guessed hidden mechanics, such as 'formal channel challenges raise risk'. They are not published rules, and they steer story choices by wording patterns. Some conflict with each other, such as 'report openly' against 'challenging rules'. This rests on invented mechanics and makes the guidance fragile when events are reworded.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the keyword lists with a short principle: pick the honest, fully-fixing, documented option, avoid hiding, blaming and shortcuts, and judge by the stat deltas the game shows after each choice. Mark every effect-direction claim as a heuristic and cut the list to 3–4 lines.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply ... **Quarterly phase: two replies in the first quarter of the run, one reply from the second on.**
weaknesses.problem: The document is long and dense, with nested conditionals (strict mode, review-month exception, stalled start, 'first matching line wins' and a Best-stat tracking note). It also carries tool-call mechanics that a flash model will struggle to follow exactly. Batching the quarterly action numbers blind from earlier menus is brittle if the menu changes. The many thresholds, such as 'Health 5 or below' and 'Dignity 4 or below', are invented margins.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the document to about half its length. Keep one priority ladder (survive, protect the review, grow), one quarterly table by level band, and one near-limit table. Drop the per-reply batching and note-format machinery, or reduce it to 'call take_action, then observe'. Re-read the menu each quarter instead of reusing remembered numbers.

weaknesses.quote: Pay rises with level, so an earlier promotion is also the main source of Wealth. ... **Review calendar.** Reviews come every six months (handbook). The handbook lists the review after the quarterly phase; in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is long and dense, with nested conditionals, a 'first matching line wins' list, a status-line scheme (Review in N / Now / Best) and repeated cross-references. A flash-class model will struggle to follow it reliably. It also states observed behaviour (review timing, 'dismissed at month 24', 'Skill, then Output lags from L4') as 'our runs' facts. These can be wrong or can change, and they blur the line between published rules and invented mechanics.
weaknesses.fix: Cut it to about half the length. Keep one priority list, one decision procedure per phase and one near-limit table. Remove the 'in our runs' claims, or mark them clearly as heuristics. Keep the review-timing note, since it is useful when the review month is ambiguous.

weaknesses.quote: Skill** rises when you use your own judgement: analyse, bring data or evidence ... **Hidden risk** ... is likely to rise with ... challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: These are detailed keyword-to-effect mappings for story options. The game does not publish them. They are hedged as 'working assumptions', but they still drive the story decisions. This is fragile when the event wording changes, and the cues can steer the agent wrong. Examples are 'rest lowers Output' and 'any formal challenge is risky'.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce them to a few principles: take no option that clearly harms Health or Dignity at a limit, avoid concealment and shortcuts, and prefer options with a visible stat gain. Tell the agent to trust the stat deltas the game shows after each choice. Drop the long lists of cue words.

weaknesses.quote: Quarterly phase: two replies in the first quarter of the run, one reply from the second on. ... Write the main-action numbers in that quarter's note (in our runs both menus list the actions in the handbook's order).
weaknesses.problem: The turn-loop mechanics are complicated and rely on assumed menu numbering and on batching several actions in one reply before seeing the menu. If the assumption is wrong, actions fail or the wrong action is picked. The fixed quarterly recipes also barely change over the 48 months (L2-3: Report, Network, Report plus Key project every quarter). They do not adapt to what the stats show, and they do not plan for the last year beyond month 48.
weaknesses.fix: Say: observe each quarter, read the menu numbers, then choose by priority (survive first, then the weakest of Skill/Network/Output). Do not batch before seeing the menu. Add a simple three-phase plan, for example early growth, mid-game promotion push, and a final-year switch to Health, Dignity and risk control starting around month 40.

weaknesses.quote: N = 6 - (current_month mod 6), and N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6. Reviews come every six months; our plan treats the month with N = 1 as the deadline for review preparation.
weaknesses.problem: The review is settled at the end of months 6, 12, 18 and so on, after that month's story events. This formula gives the review month itself N = 6, so the review-close protections in step 4 switch off for the three story events that come just before the review. The off-by-one also confuses the 'N = 1' exception in step 2.
weaknesses.fix: Define N as the number of months until the review, counting the current month: N = 0 in a review month (months 6, 12, ...), and N = 6 - (month mod 6) otherwise. Apply the review-close rules when N <= 1, so they cover both the month before the review and the review month.

weaknesses.quote: Stalled: a provisional record of an expected gain that did not show up in this run. In a quarterly phase, add `Expect S<..> N<..> O<..>`: the values the chosen action should leave, from its displayed changes.
weaknesses.problem: The Best/Expect/Stalled/Concerns bookkeeping is heavy and its conditions are unclear ('nothing else intervened', 'displayed changes', which the handbook only gives as signs). A flash model will probably miscopy or misjudge it, and the quarterly rules 5 and 6 depend on it. It also uses a lot of tokens on every note.
weaknesses.fix: Drop Expect and Stalled, or reduce them to one rule: 'If a stat has not risen over two quarters in which you invested in it, switch to the next-weakest stat.' Keep the status line to Review-in, current S/N/O/H/D/Wealth, and the last HR remark.

weaknesses.quote: Otherwise:** spend Energy on Skill, Network and Output that are not in Stalled (Prepare report materials, Network maintenance, Skill learning while Health is comfortable). Main action Apply for a key project
weaknesses.problem: The long-horizon plan is thin. There is no phasing across the 48 months (early skill/network build-up, then a promotion push timed to the half-year windows, then late-run protection of Health/Dignity/Wealth). It never uses CurrentLevelDuration or past review grades to judge whether promotion is on track, gives no numeric meaning to 'comfortable' or 'lower part', and has no plan for Wealth beyond 'avoid spending'.
weaknesses.fix: Add a short phase plan, for example: 'Months 1–18: favour Skill learning and Network to clear the early promotion bars; Months 19–42: balance Output and Network before each 6-month window, and if CurrentLevelDuration >= 12 with B or lower grades, shift Energy to the weakest of S/N/O; Months 43–48: protect Health/Dignity >= 6 and risk.' Replace the vague limits with numbers, e.g. 'Health or Dignity <= 4'.

weaknesses.quote: Friendly ("you are doing all right"): no risk action. Quiet ("some risk, nothing serious yet"): first Energy action Defuse legacy risk, main action from the lines below. Anything else (frowning, uneasy, "you are on your own", angry)
weaknesses.problem: The risk response depends on a 'monthly HR remark' and its exact wording. Neither appears in the published rules. If the phrasing changes or the remark is missing, the agent cannot tell which branch it is in, so the guidance stops working. The rules present an observed mechanic as if it were published.
weaknesses.fix: Base the risk tiers on signals the rules describe in general terms: no warning, mild or uncertain risk feedback, or a written or verbal warning or a red-line notice. Describe each tier by what it means rather than by quoted strings. Add a fallback: if no risk signal appears for two quarters, use Defuse legacy risk once every 2–3 quarters anyway.

weaknesses.quote:
Start every note with:
`Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: A flash model has to maintain five bookkeeping fields on every turn: Best per level, a provisional Stalled set with Expect values, and a Concerns counter. The note format also forces extra check_latest_logs calls. A bookkeeping mistake changes decisions (for example, a wrongly Stalled stat blocks an investment), and the overhead costs tokens without adding much robustness.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the status line to `Month M | Review in N | H D S N O W | Warning: yes/no`. Drop Best, Stalled and Expect, or make them optional. Replace them with one simple rule: if a stat did not rise after two investments in a row, switch to a different action that raises it.

weaknesses.quote: 6. **Otherwise:** spend Energy on Skill, Network and Output that are not in Stalled (Prepare report materials, Network maintenance, Skill learning while Health is comfortable). Main action Apply for a key project
weaknesses.problem: The Skill gives no plan across the 48 months beyond the review cycle and the final quarter. It does not set phase goals for months 1–12, 13–36 and 37–48, or say when to push for promotion versus consolidate. Wealth and the debt/broke direction appear only as 'avoid spending'. Skill obsolescence at higher levels is not tied to level. Thresholds such as 'lower part of its 0–10 range' are vague.
weaknesses.fix: Add a short horizon section. Early: build Skill and Network, never let Health or Dignity fall below 5. Middle: aim for a promotion at most windows by entering each window with Output and Network rising. Late: protect level, Health, Dignity and risk for the ending score. Give numeric triggers: Health or Dignity ≤4 means recover; Wealth <1 means no paid options; Wealth <0 means the debt emergency. Add a rule that after each promotion, Skill learning comes first so Skill keeps up with the new level.

weaknesses.quote:
Start every note with:
`Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The mandatory status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Expect, Concerns, Review countdown) is heavy and error-prone for a flash-class model. It relies on the agent copying the note from check_latest_logs, and 'Stalled' is a speculative inference built on noisy stat changes. This hurts clarity and robustness and adds token cost.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce it to a short note, e.g. 'Month M | Health H Dignity D | focus'. Drop Best, Stalled and Concerns, and rely on the observe stats and trends each turn.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky." and "Skill** rises when you use your own judgement: analyse, bring data or evidence...
weaknesses.problem: These are invented keyword heuristics for how story options move stats and hidden risk. They are presented as how options 'usually' move, with no hedging against the unpublished mechanics. Several are doubtful, for example 'challenging the company even through a formal channel' raising risk. A blanket 'treat as risky' bias can freeze the agent into passive choices and stall growth.
weaknesses.fix: Say that the effect text and the outcome feedback shown in the game take precedence. Keep the heuristics to a few generic ones, such as 'prefer transparent, complete fixes over concealment', and label them as unverified tendencies.

weaknesses.quote: Last quarter of the career (month 48):** plan Energy and the main action together... "In the final quarter of the career, prefer Health, Dignity and lower risk instead.
weaknesses.problem: The 48-month horizon is thin. There is no phased plan (early skill and network building, mid-game promotion pushes, late consolidation) and no use of the ending dimensions: level, wealth, skill, network, risk, health and dignity. Month 48 is also a single month, yet the endgame rule drops Skill, Output and Network growth. It also ignores that a level reached or wealth gained late is worth more than a small Health gain.
weaknesses.fix: Add explicit phases, for example months 1-12 build Skill and Network while keeping Health up, months 13-40 push for promotion each window, and months 41-48 protect the final dimensions. State how the quarterly action choice trades off against the ending score components, and keep the last-quarter rule from sacrificing the promotion window.

weaknesses.quote:
Start every note with:
`Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Expect, Concerns) is heavy and stateful. It depends on the agent copying its own earlier notes, and Stalled rests on a mechanism the game doesn't publish, since gains are noisy and have hidden causes. A weak flash model will likely drop or corrupt the state. The Stalled logic can also wrongly disable useful investments.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the status line to 'Review in N | S/N/O now'. Remove Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns. Use the observable trend in Skill, Network and Output between reviews, read from observe or check_latest_logs, to decide what to prioritise.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk** rises with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record ... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel. ... when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: It states invented keyword-to-risk mappings as fact, though the rules say hidden-risk conditions are not published. Treating formal challenges and partial fixes as risky can make the agent avoid good choices. Many of the stat-effect heuristics (for example 'Output falls when you learn') are also asserted as certain. The review-month exception that allows 'mild risk' contradicts the rest of the risk guidance.
weaknesses.fix: Label these as heuristics inferred from the handbook's red-flag wording ('hiding, shortcuts, blame'). Drop the unverified claims about formal channels and partial fixes. Remove the review-month risk exception, or say plainly that risk is always weighed first.

weaknesses.quote: Last quarter of the career (month 48): plan Energy and the main action together. ... Quarterly phases only: first matching line wins
weaknesses.problem: The 48-month plan is thin and reactive. There is no phased arc (early skill and network build, mid-game promotion pushes, late-game wealth, health and risk cleanup). Salary and level growth are ignored. Month 48 is likely not a quarterly phase with usable actions, because the run may end on the month-48 events, so the final-quarter rules may never fire. The window 'In the final quarter... prefer Health, Dignity' is vague.
weaknesses.fix: Add a short horizon plan: months 1-12 build Skill and Network, 13-36 push promotion cycles, and from month 40 onward shift to Health, Dignity and risk cleanup. Cover the month-45 quarterly phase as well as month 48. Tie Wealth to promotion, since salary rises with level.
